unstated.what: Exact serialization of 'escaped as code point': lowercase hex digits, no zero-padding, followed by a trailing space (e.g. '\x01' -> '\\1 ', '\x1f' -> '\\1f ', '\x7f' -> '\\7f ', '1abc' -> '\\31 abc')
Exact serialization of 'the escaped character': a backslash immediately followed by the character with no trailing space (e.g. '.' -> '\\.', ' ' -> '\\ ', '-' -> '\\-')
The function must be exposed as a public callable attribute of the top-level package module (``sv.escape``); the instruction says 'add escape function' but does not name the module or public API path

leading digit escaped as code point (test_escape_first_digit) and non-leading digits passed through (test_escape_non_first_digit)

identifier-safe chars (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '-', '_', >= U+0080) pass through (test_escape_underscore, test_escape_internal_dash, test_escape_high_unicode, test_escape_high_unicode_bmp, test_escape_uppercase_passthrough)

reason: The instruction quotes the full CSS escaping spec, so all behavioral rules are covered. The only unstated details are the concrete output serialization (lowercase minimal hex + space for code points, backslash+char for escaped characters) and the public module path ``sv.escape``, both of which are conventional/derivable choices a careful implementer would make.
